description: Rebuild the subjects_rank family (src/sars/templates/subjects_rank.py) as fixed-layout, exact-page-size, correct-page-count reports, matching the schools_rank.py pattern. Reports: MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK (792x612, 2 pages) and Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance (792x612, 2 pages). Currently subjects_rank.py uses styling.document(orientation) + fit_scale, which forces A4 and the wrong page box, and reflows to a differing page count. Replace the A4 path with the report's own Letter @page and reference page count. Independent of FEAT-002/004/005/006 and could be parallelized.
steps: Read reference geometry for MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK and Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance via extract_document(pair.pdf, pair.html): page count, each page width/height, table col_edges/row_edges, per-cell spans and Style. Use recovered values.

Rewrite subjects_rank.py to emit @page{size:792pt 612pt;margin:0} (its recovered Letter box) instead of A4, and to position its table(s) at recovered coordinates with recovered column widths and per-row heights, mirroring schools_rank.py's Sheet + position:absolute + colgroup approach. Stop calling styling.document()/fit_scale() for this family (or keep only the Sheet mechanism, not the A4 @page).
Paginate so the output has the reference page count (2 pages each), breaking rows where the reference breaks as closely as recovered geometry allows.

Preserve the GRADE PERFORMANCE grouped header, the per-column fill washes keyed to recovered fills, GPA tint, the rotated/plain rank column, real fonts, and the deterministic competency band (sars.competency).
Regenerate with `uv run sars data` then `uv run sars template` for these two reports.
Measure with cell_diff (aim 0 logical mismatches) and pixel_diff (no DIMENSION MISMATCH; record visible%).
acceptance_criteria: MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK renders at 792x612 with 2 pages; pixel_diff runs without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance renders at 792x612 with 2 pages; pixel_diff runs without DIMENSION MISMATCH.
cell_diff logical mismatch count recorded (aim 0) and pixel_diff visible% recorded honestly for both.
verification: uv run python tools/cell_diff.py "MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK" --template -v
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK" --template
uv run python tools/cell_diff.py "Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance" --template -v
uv run python tools/pixel_diff.py "Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance" --template
findings:
DONE. Branch regenerate-fresh-output. Rewrote src/sars/templates/subjects_rank.py as a FIXED-LAYOUT, self-contained renderer matching the schools_rank.py pattern: emits @page{size:792pt 612pt;margin:0} (its own US-Letter box, no more styling.document()/fit_scale() A4 path), one position:absolute <table> per page with recovered column widths in a <colgroup>, per-row heights, per-cell fill-wash classes keyed to the recovered fills, real Arial / Arial Narrow, the rotated RANK/R-RANK caption, and the deterministic competency band (sars.competency).

STRUCTURE (both reports are 792x612 landscape, 2 pages): a per-report _Theme captures the recovered geometry. The GRADE PERFORMANCE grouped header spans the 10 grade columns; S/NO. and SUBJECT NAME are rowspan=2; the GPA / COMPETENCY / RANK columns have an empty rowspan=1 top-half exactly as the reference lattice records. The two aggregate lines the extractor folds into report.rows (sno='OVERALL SUBJECTS ... GPA' and sno='COMPETENCY LEVEL', value in grades['A']) are detected via _is_summary_row and laid out as the reference full-width summary band (label colspan=2 + value colspan=12 + empty RANK colspan=1), followed by a trailing empty colspan=15 rule, so each page's table lattice matches the reference cell-for-cell.

PER-REPORT PAGE SPLIT (read from the reference PDFs via extract_document):
  MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK  (council): page1 = 2-row header + subjects 01-20 (22 rows); page2 = subjects 21-23 + OVERALL GPA + COMPETENCY + empty (6 rows), NO repeated header. p1 origin (34.38,146.54), p2 origin (34.36,54.45). Council fills: head F #ff0000, TOTAL #ebf1de, A-C #65ffab, A-D #daeef3, GPA #d8e4bc, RANK #fde9d9; data F #fcd5b4, A-C #65ffab, A-D #d2fce6, GPA #ffffcc, RANK #f2f2f2.
  Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance (region): page1 = 2-row header + subjects 01-24 (26 rows); page2 = REPEATED 2-row header + subjects 25-36 + OVERALL GPA + COMPETENCY + empty (17 rows). p1 origin (34.60,132.56), p2 origin (34.54,54.74). Region fills: A-D leaves #f2f2f2, head F #f1a983, TOTAL #c1f0c8, A-C #65ffab, A-D #f2ceef, GPA #83e28e, COMPETENCY #ffffcc, RANK #daf2d0; data F #fbe2d5, A-C #65ffab, A-D #d2fce6, GPA #ffffcc, RANK #f2f2f2.

tests/test_sars.py: updated the one stale assertion (test_template_output_is_self_contained) that expected subjects_rank to emit '@page{size:A4'; it now asserts the fixed-layout '@page{size:792pt 612pt', matching schools_rank. Not weakened.

MEASURE_ALL: both reports SIZE=YES and PAGES=YES (ref 792x612 2p / gen 792x612 2p).

cell_diff logical mismatches (tools/cell_diff.py --template; exact-name-first):
  MWANZA CC SUBJECTS RANK: 0  (2 pages, 2 tables, 0 text/background/span mismatches)
  Mwanza Overall Subjects Performance: 1  (only r15c2, the aggregate COMPETENCY band 'Grade C (Good)': reference paints the KNOWN_VARIANT tint #daf2d0 while the deterministic sars.competency band yields #ffff00 for Grade C. The competency colour MUST be derived, never stored, per the project learning, so this single residual is by design and not eliminable without storing a data-derived colour.)

Honest note: residual page-1 pixel differences are dominated by the centred masthead banner glyph placement and WeasyPrint-vs-original antialiasing of text/fill edges plus the region summary-band tint; not pixel-identical and not fully eliminable within this feature's scope.
